text:
mike: Ran a perfetto e2e trace for the failing workload (client->gateway->runtime) — attaching link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (sensitive view)
anya: saw this earlier — looks like kernel selection flips around the 120ms mark, and batching size oscillates
devon: can you paste the span waterfall? short clip would help.
mike: here's the key waterfall snippet (copied from perfetto flame view):
```
client.call -> gateway.recv 8ms
gateway.enqueue -> gateway.dispatch 12ms
gateway->runtime rpc 6ms
runtime.kv_cache_lookup 30ms (multiple)
runtime.kernel_select 45ms -> kernelA->kernelB flip
runtime.execute 18ms (split across kernels)
```
luis: that kernelA->kernelB flip looks like the hysteresis threshold kicking in. we lowered it in the last rollout (0.15 -> 0.05) which makes the runtime prefer a smaller kernel earlier
anya: and the KV cache lookups are spiking when the kernel flip happens — maybe cache warming is tied to kernel choice
ben: ran nsys around same time, got these aggregates:
```
Time(%) Kernel    Calls  Avg(ms)
30.2%  kernelA   124    0.36
44.8%  kernelB   98     0.78
15.1%  memcpy    210    0.12
```
mike: note that kernelB avg is ~2x; the flip increases tail latencies even though median improves for some sequence lengths
devon: any batching heuristic changes in the past week? we saw oscillation between batch sizes 1,4,8 in traces
luis: yes — experiment: adaptive_batching.max_inflight reduced from 16 -> 8 to control GPU memory. that makes the scheduler more aggressive about splitting
anya: possible interaction: smaller inflight + lower hysteresis -> runtime quickly switches to kernelB which has higher per-call overhead for small batches 
perf-bot: deploy/2026-03-10: rollout v1.12.3 (hysteresis=0.05, max_inflight=8) to staging
ben: repro steps I used: 50qps, seq_len_dist skewed to 128 tokens, run for 5m, collect perfetto + nsys at t=2m and t=4m
mike: here's a perfetto query I ran to find the flip events:
```sql
select ts, name from slice where name LIKE 'runtime.kernel_select' and dur > 10000 order by ts desc limit 50;
```
anya: results show repeated kernel_select events clustered with kv_cache_lookup spikes — could be cache eviction thrash
devon: do we have KV cache metrics (hit/miss) correlated? maybe batch boundary causes cache keys to be evicted due to memory pressure
luis: added logs to runtime to emit cache.size and cache.evictions at 1s intervals. I pushed a debug build to staging (tag: evict-debug-20260310)
ben: attaching a grep output from runtime logs around the incident:
```
[02:14:21] cache.size=512MB cache.evictions=0
[02:14:22] cache.size=480MB cache.evictions=32
[02:14:23] cache.size=512MB cache.evictions=0
[02:14:24] cache.size=476MB cache.evictions=40
```
mike: that pattern looks like periodic GC/eviction cycles — could be our prefetch/evict heuristic ping-ponging
anya: hypothesis: lower max_inflight causes more frequent smaller batches, which increases distinct key churn in cache -> evictions -> kernel flip (because kernel selection sees more cache misses and picks kernelB)
luis: action items: 1) revert hysteresis to 0.12 in staging, 2) temporarily increase max_inflight to 12 to see if batch size stabilizes, 3) run perfetto+nsys for 10m with cache.logging enabled
devon: +1. also add a perfetto track for 'cache.eviction' so it's visible in the timeline
ben: I'll run an A/B with current and reverted config, capture traces (links will be posted)
mike: if A/B shows reduced tail after revert we'll consider runtime patch: add dampening to eviction heuristic (e.g., require 3 consecutive high-eviction intervals before switching kernel)
ya: also file an eval test to synthesize the churn pattern so we catch regressions CI-side
perf-bot: test/trace-compare: queued job 9891 (will upload trace artifacts when done)
luis: timeline: will run tests at 10:30PT and attach traces here. anyone else want to be on the run?
devon: I'll join and watch perfetto live
ben: same
mike: thanks team. let's prefer short runs then a long 10m run once configs look stable. please paste perfetto links in thread. :thumbsup:
